skip_plan.drift_warning: A skipped transaction is missing on the replica. Rows it touched now differ from the source, and later transactions on those rows may fail or change different data silently.
after: Find the cause: writes run directly on the replica (check read_only and super_read_only), non-deterministic statements, or a replica restored from an inconsistent backup.

Verify the affected tables with checksums computed on both sides over the same data (CHECKSUM TABLE on a quiet table, or a chunked checksum tool in the style of pt-table-checksum). myflames recommends this and never runs it for you.
Resync those tables or rebuild the replica (clone or backup restore).
skip_plan.privileges: SET GLOBAL sql_slave_skip_counter needs SUPER; START SLAVE needs SUPER.
notes: The counter counts events, but when it reaches 1 inside an event group it keeps skipping to the end of that group, so 1 skips the rest of the current transaction; myflames only ever sets 1. It is global (no FOR CHANNEL): the START below copies it to this channel and resets it to 0.
MySQL 5.7 records no queue or apply timestamps per transaction (they arrived in MySQL 8.0), so worker lag is not shown.

Seconds_Behind_Master compares the original timestamp of the event being applied with the replica's clock, adjusted by the clock difference measured when the receiver connected. A clock change on either server after that skews it, and one long transaction shows as a jump, so it is never the only lag signal.
